key_insight: A deep learning model trained on a large expert-curated UK Biobank ECG dataset accurately measured PR, QRS, and QT intervals and outperformed existing automated methods.
clinical_relevance: More reliable ECG interval measurement could improve large-scale cardiovascular research and support better risk stratification for outcomes such as atrial fibrillation and major adverse cardiovascular events.
method: Built a reference dataset with 11,330 lead-level annotations from 1,030 UK Biobank participants.
Trained a 1D convolutional neural network to segment ECG waveforms and estimate PR, QRS, and QT intervals.
Compared performance with expert annotations, CardioSoft, an open-source toolbox, and a wavelet-based method.
evidence_signal: Inter-observer agreement was high (ICC 0.81-0.97), and the model achieved low mean absolute errors on the held-out test set: 7.7 ms for PR, 7.5 ms for QRS, and 4.9 ms for QT.
watch_item: The model was validated in UK Biobank, so external performance and generalizability to other populations, acquisition settings, and ECG systems still need confirmation.
paper_title: A curated reference dataset and deep learning model for multi-lead electrocardiographic interval measurements in UK Biobank
